citation.title: A Class of Unbiased Estimators of the Average Treatment Effect in Randomized Experiments

standing_assumptions:
Finite-population, design-based potential-outcomes setting (the Neyman-Rubin model): potential outcomes and covariates are fixed and the only randomness is the assignment of units to treatment and control. Transcribed from the page images.

(S1) Section 3, pp. 137-138 (PDF pp. 3-4): 'Define a binary treatment indicator $T_i$ for units $i = 1,2,\ldots,N$ such that $T_i = 1$ when unit $i$ receives the treatment and $T_i = 0$ otherwise. If the stable unit treatment value assumption [16] holds, let $Y_{1i}$ be the potential outcome if unit $i$ is exposed to the treatment, and let $Y_{0i}$ be the potential outcome if unit $i$ is not exposed to the treatment. The observed outcome $Y_i$ may be expressed as a function of the potential outcomes and the treatment: $Y_i = T_iY_{1i} + (1-T_i)Y_{0i}$. [1] The causal effect of the treatment on unit $i$, $\tau_i$, is defined as the difference between the two potential outcomes for unit $i$: $\tau_i \equiv Y_{1i} - Y_{0i}$. [2] The ATE, denoted by $\Delta$, is defined as the average value of $\tau_i$ for all units $i$. In the Neyman-Rubin model, the only random component is the allocation of units to treatment and control groups.' Eq. [3]: $\Delta = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\tau_i}{N} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}(Y_{1i}-Y_{0i})}{N} = \frac{1}{N}\left[\sum_{i=1}^{N}Y_{1i} - \sum_{i=1}^{N}Y_{0i}\right] = \frac{1}{N}\left[Y_1^T - Y_0^T\right]$, 'where $Y_1^T$ is the sum of the potential outcomes if in the treatment condition and $Y_0^T$ is the sum of potential outcomes if in the control condition.' Eq. [4]: $\widehat{\Delta} = \frac{1}{N}\left[\widehat{Y_1^T} - \widehat{Y_0^T}\right]$, 'where $\widehat{Y_1^T}$ is the estimated sum of potential outcomes under treatment and $\widehat{Y_0^T}$ is the estimated sum of potential outcomes under control.' Footnote 2 (p. 138): 'This assumption is made without loss of generality; multiple discrete treatments (or equivalently, some units not being sampled into either treatment or control) are easily accommodated in this framework. All instances of $(1 - T_i)$ in the text may be replaced by $C_i$, an indicator variable for whether or not unit $i$ receives the control, with one exception to be noted in Section 6.'

(S2) p. 138 (PDF p. 4): 'Formally, the bias of an estimator is the difference between the expected value of the estimator and the true parameter of interest; an estimator is unbiased if this difference is equal to zero. If the estimators $\widehat{Y_0^T}$ and $\widehat{Y_1^T}$ are unbiased, the corresponding estimator of $\Delta$ is also unbiased since $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\Delta}] = \frac{1}{N}\left[\mathrm{E}[\widehat{Y_1^T}] - \mathrm{E}[\widehat{Y_0^T}]\right] = \frac{1}{N}\left[Y_1^T - Y_0^T\right] = \Delta$.' [5]

(S3) Section 4, p. 138 (PDF p. 4): 'Define $N$ as the number of units in the study, $\pi_{1i}$ as the probability that unit $i$ is selected into treatment, and $\pi_{0i}$ as the probability that unit $i$ is selected into control. We assume that, $\forall i$, $\pi_{1i} > 0$ and $\pi_{0i} > 0$, or that there is a nonzero probability that each unit will be selected into treatment and that there is a nonzero probability that each unit will be selected into control. (When all units are assigned to either treatment or control, $\pi_{0i} + \pi_{1i} = 1$.)'

(S4) Section 5, pp. 140-141 (PDF pp. 6-7): eqs. [13]-[14], $\widehat{Y_1^{T*}} = \sum_{i=1}^{N}\left[T_i\frac{Y_{1i}}{\pi_{1i}} - T_i\frac{f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})}{\pi_{1i}} + f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})\right]$ and $\widehat{Y_0^{T*}} = \sum_{i=1}^{N}\left[(1-T_i)\frac{Y_{0i}}{\pi_{0i}} - (1-T_i)\frac{f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})}{\pi_{0i}} + f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})\right]$, 'where $f(.)$ is a predetermined real-valued function of pretreatment covariate vector $\mathbf{X_i}$ and of parameter vector $\theta_{\mathbf{i}}$'; eq. [15], $\widehat{\Delta_G} = \frac{1}{N}\left(\widehat{Y_1^{T*}} - \widehat{Y_0^{T*}}\right)$; eq. [16], $\widehat{\Delta_G} = \widehat{\Delta_{HT}} - \frac{1}{N}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}T_i\frac{f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})}{\pi_{1i}} - \sum_{i=1}^{N}(1-T_i)\frac{f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})}{\pi_{0i}}\right)$.

(S5) Section 6.1, p. 143 (PDF p. 9): '$\pi_{1i1j}$ is the probability that units $i$ and $j$ are jointly included in the treatment group'; '$\pi_{0i0j}$ is the probability that units $i$ and $j$ are jointly included in the control group'; '$\pi_{1i0j}$ is the joint probability that unit $i$ will be in the treatment group and unit $j$ will be in the control group.'

(S6) Section 6.2, pp. 143-144 (PDF pp. 9-10): 'When $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$ is constant, we may simply redefine the outcome variable, $U_i = Y_i - f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$. It follows that $U_{0i} = Y_{0i} - f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$ and $U_{1i} = Y_{1i} - f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$.' and 'As we proceed, for notational clarity, we use $Y_i$ as the outcome measure, noting that the variances derived will also apply to the generalized difference estimator if $U_i$ is substituted for $Y_i$ (along with both associated potential outcomes) and $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$ is constant.'

(S7) Section 6.3, pp. 144-145 (PDF pp. 10-11), cluster totals: 'Note that if, for some units $i,j$, $\Pr(T_i \neq T_j) = 0$, then the total estimators may be equivalently rewritten. Define $K_k \in \mathbf{K}$ as the set of unit indices $i$ that satisfy $T_i = T'_k$, where $T'_k$ is indexed over all $|\mathbf{K}|$ unique random variables in $\{T_i : i = (1,2,\ldots,N)\}$. Define $\pi'_{1k}$ as the value of $\pi_{1i}, \forall i \in K_k$, $\pi'_{0k}$ as the value of $\pi_{0i}, \forall i \in K_k$. Joint probabilities $\pi'_{1k1l}$, $\pi'_{1k0l}$, and $\pi'_{0k0l}$ are defined analogously.' With '$Y'_k = \sum_{i \in K_k} Y_i$' (p. 144) and '$Y'_{1k} = \sum_{i \in K_k} Y_{1i}$ and $Y'_{0k} = \sum_{i \in K_k} Y_{0i}$' (p. 145). The sums over clusters run over $k = 1,\ldots,M$.

(S8) Section 6.4, p. 145 (PDF p. 11): 'Our goal is now to derive conservative variance estimators: although not unbiased, these estimators are guaranteed to have a nonnegative bias.' Footnote 7: 'Although the variance estimator is nonnegatively biased, the associated standard errors may not be (due to Jensen's inequality) and any particular draw may be above or below the true value of the variance due to sampling variability.'

Reading conventions used in every target below (they follow from (S1)-(S7) in the two-arm case that the paper works in; stated here for the formalizer and flagged as conventions, not quotations): the assignment vector $(T_1,\ldots,T_N)$ has an arbitrary probability distribution on $\{0,1\}^N$ (a finite sample space), and all expectations, variances and covariances are taken over it; every unit is assigned to treatment or control, so $\pi_{1i} = \Pr(T_i = 1)$, $\pi_{0i} = \Pr(T_i = 0) = 1 - \pi_{1i}$, $\pi_{1i1j} = \Pr(T_i = 1, T_j = 1)$, $\pi_{0i0j} = \Pr(T_i = 0, T_j = 0)$, $\pi_{1i0j} = \Pr(T_i = 1, T_j = 0)$, hence $\pi_{1i1i} = \pi_{1i}$, $\pi_{0i0i} = \pi_{0i}$ and $\pi_{1i0i} = 0$, and likewise for the primed cluster quantities; the clusters $K_1,\ldots,K_M$ partition $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, $T_i = T'_k$ for every $i \in K_k$, and distinct clusters have distinct indicators, $\Pr(T'_k \neq T'_l) > 0$ for $k \neq l$; every double sum over $k, l$ (or $i, j$) is over ordered pairs; 'the sharp null hypothesis of no treatment effect whatsoever' means $Y_{1i} = Y_{0i}$ for every unit $i$.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Section 6.3, sentence before eq. [30] ('Since, for all pairs k,l such that k != l, Pr(T'_k != T'_l) > 0, then pi'_{1k0l} > 0 for all l != k'), and the claims that rest on it: eq. [34] is nonpositively biased, eq. [35] is conservative, and eq. [35] is exactly unbiased under the sharp null; as printed
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Cluster notation: Section 6.3, p. 144 (PDF p. 10), quoted in standing assumption (S7); cluster-level HT totals $\widehat{Y^T_{1,HT}} = \sum_{i=1}^{N}\frac{1}{\pi_{1i}}T_iY_i = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\sum_{i\in K_k}\frac{1}{\pi_{1i}}T_iY_i = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\sum_{i\in K_k}\frac{1}{\pi'_{1k}}T'_kY_i = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\frac{1}{\pi'_{1k}}T'_k\sum_{i\in K_k}Y_i = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\frac{1}{\pi'_{1k}}T'_kY'_k$ (p. 144, with $\pi_{1i}$ in the first sum; see P026-T10) and $\widehat{Y^T_{0,HT}} = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\frac{1}{\pi'_{0k}}(1-T'_k)Y'_k$ (p. 145, PDF p. 11); '$Y'_{1k} = \sum_{i\in K_k}Y_{1i}$ and $Y'_{0k} = \sum_{i\in K_k}Y_{0i}$' (p. 145). Eq. [34], p. 146 (PDF p. 12): $\widehat{\mathrm{Cov}}_C\left(\widehat{Y_1^T},\widehat{Y_0^T}\right) = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\sum_{l\neq k}\frac{T'_k(1-T'_l)}{\pi'_{1k0l}}(\pi'_{1k0l}-\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{0l})\frac{Y'_kY'_l}{\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{0l}} - \sum_{k=1}^{M}T'_k\frac{(Y'_k)^2}{2\pi'_{1k}} - \sum_{k=1}^{M}(1-T'_k)\frac{(Y'_k)^2}{2\pi'_{0k}}$. Eq. [35], p. 147 (PDF p. 13): $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT}) = \frac{1}{N^2}\sum_{k=1}^{M}\Bigg[T'_k\left(\frac{Y'_k}{\pi'_{1k}}\right)^2 + (1-T'_k)\left(\frac{Y'_k}{\pi'_{0k}}\right)^2 + \sum_{l\neq k}\Bigg(\frac{T'_kT'_l}{\pi'_{1k1l}+\varepsilon_{1k1l}}(\pi'_{1k1l}-\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{1l})\frac{Y'_k}{\pi'_{1k}}\frac{Y'_l}{\pi'_{1l}} + \frac{(1-T'_k)(1-T'_l)}{\pi'_{0k0l}+\varepsilon_{0k0l}}(\pi'_{0k0l}-\pi'_{0k}\pi'_{0l})\frac{Y'_k}{\pi'_{0k}}\frac{Y'_l}{\pi'_{0l}} - 2\frac{T'_k(1-T'_l)}{\pi'_{1k0l}+\varepsilon_{1k0l}}(\pi'_{1k0l}-\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{0l})\frac{Y'_kY'_l}{\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{0l}}\Bigg) + \sum_{\forall l:\pi'_{1k1l}=0}\left(T'_k\frac{(Y'_k)^2}{2\pi'_{1k}} + T'_l\frac{(Y'_l)^2}{2\pi'_{1l}}\right) + \sum_{\forall l:\pi'_{0k0l}=0}\left((1-T'_k)\frac{(Y'_k)^2}{2\pi'_{0k}} + (1-T'_l)\frac{(Y'_l)^2}{2\pi'_{0l}}\right)\Bigg]$, 'where $\varepsilon_{akbl} = 1[\pi'_{akbl} = 0]$. ($\varepsilon_{akbl}$ is included to avoid division by zero.)' Conservative means nonnegatively biased: Section 6.4, p. 145, quoted in standing assumption (S8). In both counterexamples each cluster is one unit, so $Y'_k = Y_k$, $\pi'_{1k} = \pi_{1k}$ and $N = M$.
canonical_claim.note: Counterexample A is the two-unit design given by both fresh readers and re-derived by the validators; B is the adjudicator's design (validate/P026-E002/adjudicate/artifact/derivation.md, section 2, and exact-output.txt). All numbers were recomputed independently in exact arithmetic when this target was fixed. In eq. [35] the sums '$\forall l : \pi'_{1k1l} = 0$' and '$\forall l : \pi'_{0k0l} = 0$' are empty in both examples. The general identity behind the numbers is part (c) of P026-T2.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Section 6.3 (sentence before eq. [30]) and Section 6.4 (eqs. [34], [35], the sentences after them, footnote 9), corrected by adding the missing bound for cluster pairs with pi'_{1k0l} = 0; no design assumption is added
canonical_claim.location: p. 145 (PDF p. 11); pp. 146-147 (PDF pp. 12-13); Appendix E, p. 152 (PDF p. 18)
canonical_claim.statement:
Corrected statement (the repair selected in the adjudicated verdict: the estimators are changed and the claim keeps its scope of arbitrary designs).

Setting (Section 6.3 with the standing assumptions): $M$ clusters with assignment indicators $T'_1,\ldots,T'_M \in \{0,1\}$ following an arbitrary probability distribution on $\{0,1\}^M$; $\pi'_{1k} = \Pr(T'_k = 1) > 0$ and $\pi'_{0k} = \Pr(T'_k = 0) = 1 - \pi'_{1k} > 0$ for every $k$; $\pi'_{1k1l} = \Pr(T'_k = 1, T'_l = 1)$, $\pi'_{0k0l} = \Pr(T'_k = 0, T'_l = 0)$, $\pi'_{1k0l} = \Pr(T'_k = 1, T'_l = 0)$; fixed real cluster totals $Y'_{1k}$ and $Y'_{0k}$; observed total $Y'_k = T'_kY'_{1k} + (1 - T'_k)Y'_{0k}$; $N \geq 1$ the number of units; $\widehat{Y_1^T} = \sum_{k=1}^{M} T'_kY'_k/\pi'_{1k}$, $\widehat{Y_0^T} = \sum_{k=1}^{M}(1 - T'_k)Y'_k/\pi'_{0k}$ and $\widehat{\Delta}_{HT} = (\widehat{Y_1^T} - \widehat{Y_0^T})/N$. All double sums are over ordered pairs. Write $Z_{11} = \{(k,l) : k \neq l,\ \pi'_{1k1l} = 0\}$, $Z_{00} = \{(k,l) : k \neq l,\ \pi'_{0k0l} = 0\}$ and $Z_{10} = \{(k,l) : k \neq l,\ \pi'_{1k0l} = 0\}$.

(a) (Replaces the deduction printed before eq. [30].) For all $k \neq l$, $\Pr(T'_k \neq T'_l) = \pi'_{1k0l} + \pi'_{1l0k}$. Hence $\Pr(T'_k \neq T'_l) > 0$ if and only if at least one of $\pi'_{1k0l}$, $\pi'_{1l0k}$ is positive; it does not imply $\pi'_{1k0l} > 0$, and $Z_{10}$ may be nonempty (P026-T1).
(b) (Eq. [30] is kept.) In every design of the setting, including those with $Z_{10} \neq \emptyset$: $\mathrm{Cov}\left(\widehat{Y_1^T},\widehat{Y_0^T}\right) = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\sum_{l\neq k}(\pi'_{1k0l}-\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{0l})\frac{Y'_{1k}Y'_{0l}}{\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{0l}} - \sum_{k=1}^{M}Y'_{1k}Y'_{0k}$.
(c) (Exact bias of the estimator printed as eq. [35], with its $\varepsilon$ convention.) $N^2\left\{\mathrm{E}\left[\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT})\right] - \mathrm{Var}(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT})\right\} = \sum_{k=1}^{M}(Y'_{1k} - Y'_{0k})^2 + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{(k,l)\in Z_{11}}(Y'_{1k} + Y'_{1l})^2 + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{(k,l)\in Z_{00}}(Y'_{0k} + Y'_{0l})^2 - 2\sum_{(k,l)\in Z_{10}}Y'_{1k}Y'_{0l}$. The last sum has no sign, which is why eq. [35] can be biased downward.
(d) (Corrected covariance estimator, replacing eq. [34].) Define $\widehat{\mathrm{Cov}}^{+}_C\left(\widehat{Y_1^T},\widehat{Y_0^T}\right) = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\sum_{l\neq k:\pi'_{1k0l}>0}\frac{T'_k(1-T'_l)}{\pi'_{1k0l}}(\pi'_{1k0l}-\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{0l})\frac{Y'_kY'_l}{\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{0l}} - \sum_{k=1}^{M}T'_k\frac{(Y'_k)^2}{2\pi'_{1k}} - \sum_{k=1}^{M}(1-T'_k)\frac{(Y'_k)^2}{2\pi'_{0k}} - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{(k,l)\in Z_{10}}\left\{T'_k\frac{(Y'_k)^2}{\pi'_{1k}} + (1-T'_l)\frac{(Y'_l)^2}{\pi'_{0l}}\right\}$. Then $\mathrm{E}\left[\widehat{\mathrm{Cov}}^{+}_C\left(\widehat{Y_1^T},\widehat{Y_0^T}\right)\right] - \mathrm{Cov}\left(\widehat{Y_1^T},\widehat{Y_0^T}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k=1}^{M}(Y'_{1k} - Y'_{0k})^2 - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{(k,l)\in Z_{10}}(Y'_{1k} - Y'_{0l})^2 \leq 0$.
(e) (Corrected variance estimator, replacing eq. [35].) Define $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}^{+}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT}) = \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT}) + \frac{1}{N^2}\sum_{(k,l)\in Z_{10}}\left\{T'_k\frac{(Y'_k)^2}{\pi'_{1k}} + (1-T'_l)\frac{(Y'_l)^2}{\pi'_{0l}}\right\}$, where $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT})$ is eq. [35] as printed; on every assignment of positive probability this equals $N^{-2}\left(\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{Y_1^T}) + \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{Y_0^T}) - 2\widehat{\mathrm{Cov}}^{+}_C(\widehat{Y_1^T},\widehat{Y_0^T})\right)$ with eqs. [32] and [33]. Then $N^2\left\{\mathrm{E}\left[\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}^{+}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT})\right] - \mathrm{Var}(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT})\right\} = \sum_{k=1}^{M}(Y'_{1k} - Y'_{0k})^2 + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{(k,l)\in Z_{11}}(Y'_{1k} + Y'_{1l})^2 + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{(k,l)\in Z_{00}}(Y'_{0k} + Y'_{0l})^2 + \sum_{(k,l)\in Z_{10}}(Y'_{1k} - Y'_{0l})^2 \geq 0$. In particular $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}^{+}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT})$ is conservative (nonnegatively biased) in every design of the setting, with no positivity assumption on any joint probability and no sign restriction on the outcomes.
(f) (Sharp null; replaces the sentence after eq. [35].) If $Y'_{1k} = Y'_{0k} = c_k$ for all $k$, and $\pi'_{1k1l} > 0$ and $\pi'_{0k0l} > 0$ for all $k \neq l$, then $\mathrm{E}\left[\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}^{+}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT})\right] - \mathrm{Var}(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT}) = \frac{1}{N^2}\sum_{(k,l)\in Z_{10}}(c_k - c_l)^2$. So under these hypotheses the corrected estimator is exactly unbiased if and only if $c_k = c_l$ for every $(k,l) \in Z_{10}$; in particular it is exactly unbiased when $Z_{10} = \emptyset$. The qualification cannot be dropped: in the design of counterexample B of P026-T1 with $Y'_{1k} = Y'_{0k} = c_k$, $c = (1,2,1,1,1,1)$, one has $\mathrm{Var}(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT}) = 2759/12600$, $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT})] = 151/1400$ (eq. [35] as printed; bias $-1/9$) and $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}^{+}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_{HT})] = 3109/12600$ (bias $+1/36 = (1-2)^2/6^2$).
(g) (Generalized difference estimator; replaces the last sentence of footnote 9.) If $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$ is constant across randomizations, (a)-(f) hold with $U_i = Y_i - f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$, $U_{1i}$, $U_{0i}$ and their cluster totals in place of $Y_i$, $Y_{1i}$, $Y_{0i}$ and theirs, and with $\widehat{\Delta}_G$ in place of $\widehat{\Delta}_{HT}$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Cluster notation and the cluster-level HT totals $\widehat{Y_1^T}$, $\widehat{Y_0^T}$: standing assumption (S7) and the definitions of P026-T1. Eq. [32], p. 146 (PDF p. 12): $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{Y_1^T}) = \sum_{k=1}^{M}T'_k(1-\pi'_{1k})\left(\frac{Y'_k}{\pi'_{1k}}\right)^2 + \sum_{k=1}^{M}\sum_{l\neq k:\pi'_{1k1l}>0}\frac{T'_kT'_l}{\pi'_{1k1l}}(\pi'_{1k1l}-\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{1l})\frac{Y'_k}{\pi'_{1k}}\frac{Y'_l}{\pi'_{1l}} + \sum_{k=1}^{M}\sum_{\forall l:\pi'_{1k1l}=0}\left(T'_k\frac{(Y'_k)^2}{2\pi'_{1k}} + T'_l\frac{(Y'_l)^2}{2\pi'_{1l}}\right)$. Eq. [33], p. 146 (PDF p. 12): $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{Y_0^T}) = \sum_{k=1}^{M}(1-T'_k)(1-\pi'_{0k})\left(\frac{Y'_k}{\pi'_{0k}}\right)^2 + \sum_{k=1}^{M}\sum_{l\neq k:\pi'_{0k0l}>0}\frac{(1-T'_k)(1-T'_l)}{\pi'_{0k0l}}(\pi'_{0k0l}-\pi'_{0k}\pi'_{0l})\frac{Y'_k}{\pi'_{0k}}\frac{Y'_l}{\pi'_{0l}} + \sum_{k=1}^{M}\sum_{\forall l:\pi'_{0k0l}=0}\left((1-T'_k)\frac{(Y'_k)^2}{2\pi'_{0k}} + (1-T'_l)\frac{(Y'_l)^2}{2\pi'_{0l}}\right)$. Eqs. [34] and [35], with the $\varepsilon$ convention of eq. [35]: transcribed in the definitions of P026-T1. Residual outcomes $U_i$, $U_{1i}$, $U_{0i}$: Section 6.2, pp. 143-144, quoted in standing assumption (S6); eq. [25], p. 144 (PDF p. 10): $\widehat{\Delta_G} = \frac{1}{N}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}T_i\frac{Y_{1i}}{\pi_{1i}} - \sum_{i=1}^{N}T_i\frac{f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})}{\pi_{1i}} - \sum_{i=1}^{N}(1-T_i)\frac{Y_{0i}}{\pi_{0i}} + \sum_{i=1}^{N}(1-T_i)\frac{f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})}{\pi_{0i}}\right) = \frac{1}{N}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}T_i\frac{Y_{1i}-f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})}{\pi_{1i}} - \sum_{i=1}^{N}(1-T_i)\frac{Y_{0i}-f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})}{\pi_{0i}}\right) = \frac{1}{N}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{N}\frac{1}{\pi_{1i}}T_iU_i - \sum_{i=1}^{N}\frac{1}{\pi_{0i}}(1-T_i)U_i\right)$. Footnote 9, p. 147 (PDF p. 13): '$\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_G)$, the variance estimator as applied to $U_i$, is not generally guaranteed to be conservative. Specifically, when $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$ not constant, there is no guarantee that $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_G)$ will be conservative, though an analogy to linearized estimators suggests that it should be approximately conservative with large $N$. Importantly, however, when, for all $k,l$, $\pi'_{1k1l} > 0$ and $\pi'_{0k0l} > 0$ and the sharp null hypothesis of no treatment effect holds, $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}_C(\widehat{\Delta}_G)$ is unbiased for $\mathrm{Var}(\widehat{\Delta}_G)$.'
canonical_claim.note: From Sol's smallest_repair for P026-E002 in validated.json ('restrict [34]'s off-diagonal observable sum to pi'_{1k0l} > 0 and subtract one half of the sum, over ordered k != l with pi'_{1k0l} = 0, of {T'_k (Y'_k)^2/pi'_{1k} + (1 - T'_l)(Y'_l)^2/pi'_{0l}}. Equivalently add N^(-2) times that sum to [35] ... Under the sharp null and positive same-arm joints, state exact equality only when the cluster totals agree across every unavailable directed pair') and from equations (3)-(8) of the adjudication derivation. Identities (c), (d), (e) were also checked in exact arithmetic on several hundred random designs when this target was fixed. The other valid repair (keep eqs. [34]-[35], add an assumption) is P026-T3.

[35] with the sentences after it and footnote 9, and the scope claim 'conservative for any experimental design' (p. 137), corrected by adding the missing hypothesis pi'_{1k0l} > 0 for all pairs of distinct clusters; eqs. [34] and [35] are kept as printed
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Cluster notation and the cluster-level HT totals $\widehat{Y_1^T}$, $\widehat{Y_0^T}$: standing assumption (S7) and the definitions of P026-T1. Eqs. [34] and [35], with the $\varepsilon$ convention of eq. [35]: transcribed in the definitions of P026-T1. Eq. [30], p. 145 (PDF p. 11): $\mathrm{Cov}\left(\widehat{Y_1^T},\widehat{Y_0^T}\right) = \sum_{k=1}^{M}\sum_{l\neq k}(\pi'_{1k0l}-\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{0l})\frac{Y'_{1k}Y'_{0l}}{\pi'_{1k}\pi'_{0l}} - \sum_{k=1}^{M}Y'_{1k}Y'_{0k}$. p. 137 (PDF p. 3) as printed: 'Our article extends this prior work by proposing a new Horvitz-Thompson-based variance estimator that is conservative for any experimental design, though additional regularity conditions would be required for use in constructing confidence intervals and hypothesis tests.' canonical_claim.note: From the second route in Sol's smallest_repair for P026-E002 ('An alternative short textual repair assumes pi'_{1k0l} > 0 for every k != l, retains [34]-[35], and restricts the arbitrary-design claims') and section 5 of the adjudication derivation. canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Section 5.1, second option for deriving theta_i, and footnote 5, corrected: independence of T_i from the whole vector of assignments used in the fit
canonical_claim.statement:
Corrected statement. Setting: the standing assumptions; $N$ units with assignment vector $(T_1,\ldots,T_N)$ of arbitrary distribution on $\{0,1\}^N$ with $\pi_{1i} > 0$ and $\pi_{0i} > 0$; fixed potential outcomes with $Y_j = T_jY_{1j} + (1-T_j)Y_{0j}$; fixed covariates; $f$ a fixed real-valued function. For a unit $i$ fix an index set $J_i \subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ and a deterministic function $G_i$ (which may depend on fixed pretreatment quantities), and let $\theta_{\mathbf{i}} = G_i\left((Y_j)_{j\in J_i}\right)$.
(a) If $T_i$ is independent of the random vector $(T_j)_{j\in J_i}$ (jointly, not only of each $T_j$ separately), then $T_i \perp\!\!\!\perp \theta_{\mathbf{i}}$, $T_i \perp\!\!\!\perp f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$ and $\mathrm{Cov}(T_i,f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})) = 0$. The same conclusions hold under the weaker premise that $T_i$ is independent of the random vector $(Y_j)_{j\in J_i}$.
(b) Consequently, if the premise of (a) holds for every unit $i$, then $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{Y_1^{T*}}] = Y_1^T$, $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{Y_0^{T*}}] = Y_0^T$ and $\mathrm{E}[\widehat{\Delta_G}] = \Delta$ (Appendix B).
(c) Footnote 5 corrected: let $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}}) = f\left(\mathbf{X_i},g\left(\mathbf{Z},(Y_j)_{j\in J_i}\right)\right) = f\left(\mathbf{X_i},g\left(\mathbf{Z},(h(Y_{0j},Y_{1j},T_j))_{j\in J_i}\right)\right)$, so that $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})$ equals some function $f'\left((T_j)_{j\in J_i}\right)$; $T_i \perp\!\!\!\perp (T_j)_{j\in J_i}$ implies $T_i \perp\!\!\!\perp f'\left((T_j)_{j\in J_i}\right)$, which implies $\mathrm{Cov}(T_i,f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})) = 0$. The footnote's argument as printed is this statement for a one-element $J_i$, and is not without loss of generality.
(d) What the printed pairwise condition does give: if $T_i \perp\!\!\!\perp T_j$ for each $j \in J_i$ separately and the prediction is additive in the outcomes with fixed coefficients, $f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}}) = a_i + \sum_{j\in J_i}b_{ij}Y_j$, then $\mathrm{Cov}(T_i,f(\mathbf{X_i},\theta_{\mathbf{i}})) = \sum_{j\in J_i}b_{ij}(Y_{1j} - Y_{0j})\mathrm{Cov}(T_i,T_j) = 0$. Without additivity the pairwise condition is not sufficient (P026-T4).
(e) The paper's two examples satisfy the premise of (a): if the $T_j$ are mutually independent, $T_i$ is independent of $(T_j)_{j\neq i}$ (leave-one-out fits); if the assignment vectors of different blocks are independent, $T_i$ is independent of $(T_j)_{j \text{ not in the block of } i}$ (fits on the other blocks).
